unruled:ny_city_rs#1.1.evidence: ny_it201i p. 4, Item A: "One spouse is a New York State resident and the other is a nonresident or part-year resident. In this case, you must either: file separate New York returns ... or file jointly, as if you both were New York State residents". A joint federal return reaches this only through ny_it201.ask.spouse_resident ('Did your husband or wife also live in New York City for all of 2025?', asked on a joint return): a No makes ny_it201.spouse_not_resident true, and ny_it201.gate.spouse_nonresident (a choice on f1040.status: mfj reads spouse_not_resident; single, mfs, hoh and qss give no) refuses ny_it201.line1 ('Separate New York returns, or a joint return taxing both as residents'); a refused IT-201 is a refused New York profile, so the status item of this form is never produced for that case. A federal separate return keeps New York status 3, which the exception does not change.

unruled:ny_it2#1.1.evidence: ny_it201i p. 21: "If you received foreign income but did not receive a federal Form W-2, you must complete Form IT-2" (ny_it2 p. 2: "foreign earned income"). Form IT-2 is the wage and withholding record. Wages with no W-2 are refused federally: scope.pay_no_w2 ('wages, tips or strike benefits that are not on a W-2') leads to scope.wages_no_form ('did an employer pay you ... wages for which you have no W-2, other than the kinds of pay just asked about?'), whose Yes (scope.wages_no_form_if_pay) is in scope.other_income, which refuses; a nonresident alien is refused by the same line (scope.nonresident_if_noncitizen). So no W-2-less foreign wages reach New York and no W-2-less IT-2 record is needed; self-employment income is not wages and goes on Schedule C, not Form IT-2. As BUG-0749 (c) records.

unruled:ny_it201#1.1.evidence: The encoding is ny_it201.line37 = subtract_floor0(line35, line36), so a negative result is $0 and line 38 copies it; the note on line 37 says 'a blank is read as zero', matching ny_it201i p. 11 'If line 36 is more than line 35, leave line 37 and line 38 blank'.

unruled:ny_it201#1.2.evidence: The Line 47 worksheet is for a filer who contributed to a Charitable Gifts Trust Fund account 'and' claimed an itemized deduction for it on Form IT-196 (ny_it201i p. 13; worksheet line 4 'Enter your itemized deduction amount (Form IT-201, line 34)'). Itemizing is refused: ny_it201.gate.itemize refuses ny_it201.line34 (Form IT-196), so a standard-deduction filer takes the 'No' path 'enter the line 38 amount on line 47'.

unruled:ny_it201#1.3.evidence: ny_it201.line48 has the guard ny_it201.item_c = true then ny_it201.zero, matching ny_it201i p. 13 'If you marked the Yes box at item C... you do not qualify for this credit'; the reviewer missed it.

unruled:ny_it201#1.4.evidence: ny_it201.line69a has the guard ny_it201.item_c = true then ny_it201.zero_stc (and the $500,000 refusal), matching ny_it201i p. 20 'you marked Yes at item C... or your income... is more than $500,000, you do not qualify'; the reviewer read only the refusal gate.

unruled:ny_it201#1.5.evidence: The tool is only for full-year New York City residents (ny_it201.gate.part_year_city), whose locality is New York City: 'its rate of tax is higher than the rate of tax originally paid' (ny_it201i p. 18) is the help 'Count a purchase taxed below New York City's rate' in ny_it201.ask.bought_untaxed. The IT-135 trigger (line 59 of $1,700 or more) cannot arise: the chart amount is at most $125 (ny_it201.sut.cap) and an item of $1,000 or more is refused by ny_it201.gate.use_tax_st141.

unruled:ny_it201#1.6.evidence: The Form IT-280 election disclaims a spouse's debt after the return is processed (ny_it201i p. 22: 'complete Form IT-280... and submit it with your original return'); it changes how the refund is applied, not any IT-201 line amount, and it cannot reach IRS or other-state debts. No encoded line value changes.

unruled:ny_it201#1.7.evidence: Innocent spouse relief is requested on Form IT-285 after filing (ny_it201i p. 32: 'Do not file Form IT-285 with your return'); it does not change any amount on Form IT-201 line 80.

unruled:ny_it201#1.8.evidence: ny_it201i p. 5 says 'In most cases, you must use the same filing status you used on your federal return' and the unknown-whereabouts and refusing-spouse exceptions say 'you may file a separate New York return'; they are optional alternatives to the federal status the tool uses (f1040.status, with ny_it201.gate.spouse_nonresident for a nonresident spouse), so the tool's joint return stays valid and no amount is wrong.
